newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo '97 farm and food exports $650 mln -institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo '97 farm and food exports $650 mln -institute.

text.p: Yugoslav agriculture and food industries exports this year would be below the target and could reach $600-650 million, the Belgrade-based Institute for Foreign Trade said on Tuesday.
"It is necessary for the government to revise its plan of exporting agriculture and food industries products at the value of $729 million this year," institute economist Vojislav Stankovic said.
"We estimate exports (of agricultural products and food industries) not to be more than $650 million," he said at a news conference.
Stankovic explained the forecast was based on first crop estimations for this years harvest.
The official statistics estimated wheat production at around 2.8 million tonnes from this year's wheat acreage of 801,282 hectares.
According to Stankovic, the country needs between 2.4-2.5 million tonnes of wheat for domestic consumption which would leave only some 300,000-400,000 tonnes for exports.

He said that first forecast for maize production on 1.435 million ha sown was put at 5.8 million tonnes. Domestic market needs are estimated at 5.1-5.2 million tonnes which would leave only some 600,000 tonnes for exports.

Sunflower and soybean planted at some 170,222 ha and 69,867 ha along with last year's stocks would just be enough to meet domestic demand, Stankovic said and added: "But nothing will be left for exports."
The same is with sugarbeet sown on only some 58,171 ha out of a 100,000 ha planned.
"This year's crop, reserves and imported raw sugar will just meet domestic consumption of white sugar estimated at some 300,000 tonnes," Stankovic said.
Fruit and vegetable production which due to bad weather and frost was estimated to fall by 30 percent could secure some $160-162 million from exports, he said.

According to the Institute's latest report, January-May agriculutre and food exports stood at $188.1 million, accounting for only 21.8 percent of the total commodity exports, but only some 25.8 percent of the targeted $729 million in 1997.
Imports of food and agricultural products in the same period were worth $266.7 million or 15.6 percent of commodity imports.
